With spring just around the corner, now is the perfect time to refresh, reset, and spruce up your space. But don’t worry—spring cleaning doesn’t have to mean an entire weekend lost to scrubbing. With a trio of Trader Joe’s essentials, clearing the clutter, banishing the dust, wiping up spills, and brightening things up is as easy as, well... counting to three! 

Ready to make your room(s) sparkle? 1, 2, 3... Tidy Up!

Even the soggiest of spills and messiest of messes are no match for Trader Joe’s Reusable Sponge Cloths. Made with a feel-it-to-believe-it, soft-yet-sturdy blend of 70% cellulose and 30% cotton, these Cloths are impressively absorbent, making them excellent, eco-friendly alternatives to paper towels. 

They’re also magnificently low maintenance; once you’ve finished tidying up, rinse them out, lay them flat to dry, and they’re ready to reuse. If they need a little cleaning, simply toss them in your washing machine or dishwasher with a normal load, and—presto! Good as new.

With a 2.4% hydrogen peroxide solution as its active ingredient, Trader Joe’s Fresh Citrus All-Purpose Disinfectant Cleaner is adept at dealing with everything from tough grease stains in the kitchen to mold and mildew in the bathroom. 

Not only does it kill 99.9% of common household bacteria and viruses on all sorts of surfaces, but it does so without the use of harsh, lung-irritating chemicals like chlorine bleach, phosphates, and sodium laureth sulfate—and leaves behind a refreshing citrus scent, to boot!

Nothing ties a newly-tidied room together quite like a big bunch of daffodils—and the value on Trader Joe's Daffodils can’t be beat! For a mighty sunny price, you get a 15 (FIFTEEN!) stem bunch of what will become some of the brightest and most beautiful blooms you ever did see. 

We sell these beauties unopened; simply trim their stems when you get home, place them in water, and wait a day or two for your flowers to unfurl! (Check out our video guide to How to Do Right By Your Daffodils for maximum enjoyment.) Now... sit back, relax, and enjoy those fresh, clean vibes!

At Trader Joe’s, we’re firm believers in the idea that making a scrumptious, satisfying meal shouldn’t be an astronomically expensive endeavor—nor does it need to be as complicated as rocket science. In fact, we've found that some of the best recipes out there are also the simplest, requiring only a handful of ingredients and minimal prep work.

So in the spirit of effortless, affordable eating, we’ve dedicated this space to some of our favorite dishes that can be completed in just three small steps. Talk about a giant leap for mealtime!

Read on to discover four options, including easy entrées and stellar snacks, each with an ingredient list designed to cost about $10—save for a few pantry essentials like butter, oil, or salt. With these recipes at the ready, it’s never been easier to launch your cooking to an exciting new frontier. And all for a decidedly down-to-Earth price, too.

We’re over the moon for our Mini Chicken Cilantro Wontons in pretty much any context, but as the centerpiece of a sweet and spicy stir fry dish, they shine brighter than the sun. And best of all, this dish only requires a quick Chop, Steam, and Stir-Fry to put it all together.

Start by giving our Baby Bok Choy a nice Chop (into halves or quarters, depending on how big you like them), then Steam the Mini Wontons on the stovetop. Once those are ready, Stir-Fry the Bok Choy, add in the Broccoli Slaw, Wontons, and a bit of General Tsao Stir Fry Sauce, and you’ve got a hearty, satisfying entrée that’ll have you roving for seconds.

blocks.description: Our Chicken Cilantro Mini Wontons are delicious enough on their own as an appetizer or snack, but when placed as the centerpiece of a sweet and spicy stir fry, they truly shine—especially when they’re allowed to brown on the bottom prior to steaming. Combine that with the crunchy, satisfying texture of our Organic Broccoli Slaw and Baby Bok Choy, and you’ve got an easy, satisfying entrée that’ll keep your guests coming back for seconds.
blocks.title: Mini Chicken Wonton Stir Fry

blocks.html:
Astronauts appreciate the advantages of canned food, but here on earth, canned cuisine sometimes gets a bad rap. Fortunately, Trader Joe's Giant Baked Beans in Tomato Sauce should impress any earthling in this meatless meal that's made with an almost simultaneous Roast, Boil, and Sauté. 

Roast Mini Pearl Tomatoes in a 400°F oven, while a pot of salted water comes to Boil for your Penne Rigate. While you’re waiting for the tomatoes and pasta to finish, Sauté Garlic and Kale with olive oil, adding a can of Giant Baked Beans once the Kale is reduced. Mix the roasted Tomatoes and Penne in—then serve sprinkled with Parmesan to any space travelers and aliens who may have found their way to your table.

blocks.description:
If you’ve never liked baked beans, this may be your bridge to bean bliss! The dish is a riff on Tuscan white bean, kale, and sausage soup. Except... it’s not soup—it’s a hearty bowl of pasta. And, there’s no meat. Briefly roasting the Grape Tomatoes adds serious depth of flavor, and our Giant Baked Beans in Tomato Sauce really satisfy, with their dense, meaty texture and flavorful Mediterranean Herbs and Spices.

Tip: You won’t need the whole pound of Penne Rigate to match the proportions of the other ingredients, but you can pad the pot with more pasta if you’re feeding a group—or a few, really hungry people.
blocks.title: Vegan Giant Bean & Kale Penne

blocks.html:
It’s a big planet with a sprawling universe of food traditions. To celebrate them all, you might need to get creative—like this Dip, Zap, Wrap that makes a multicultural sammie substitute! By Dip, we mean to make an Indian-style raita using Greek Nonfat Plain Yogurt, shredded Cucumber, diced Jalapeño, and some spices. Then Zap our Vegetable Biryani in the microwave on high for 2-3 minutes.

Finally, Wrap some Biryani in a large TJ’s Tortilla (be sure to include 2-3 dumplings with the rice and veggies), along with a healthy dollop of homemade cucumber raita, plus fresh cilantro, if you like. One bite of this mouthwatering mashup will transport you all the way around the world and beyond!

blocks.description:
If you’re in the mood for a multicultural culinary mashup, this handy, flavorful, sammie substitute with a touch of Indian fare flair may be just the thing! Start with a simple homemade raita with Greek Nonfat Plain Yogurt, shredded Cucumber, diced Jalapeño, and spices. Then microwave the Vegetable Biryani for 2-3 minutes, and wrap a couple spoonfuls, along with a dollop of raita, in a large TJ’s Tortilla.

Tip: One package of Biryani can make 2-3 burritos. Be sure to evenly divide the dumplings between them.
blocks.title: Veggie Biryani Burritos

blocks.html:
A good grilled cheese has near-universal appeal, especially when accentuated by the peppery notes of our Pimento Cheese Dip and fiery fun of our Hot & Sweet Jalapeños. And all it takes from you is quick Spread, Stack, and Sizzle. First, Spread a generous layer of Pimento Cheese on two slices of Sourdough Bread, then Stack as many Jalapeños as you see fit onto one slice (one or two for a mild pop of flavor, or cover the whole surface for some supernova-level heat).

Then, simply Sizzle on both sides in a well-buttered skillet until browned and melty. It might just be the quickest, easiest, and tastiest lunch option you’ll find this side of the Milky Way.

blocks.description: Our rich, peppery Pimento Cheese Dip and Hot & Sweet Jalapeños co-star in this fun and fiery (and super easy-to-make) grilled cheese, which can easily be adjusted to your preferred level of heat by simply adding more or fewer jalapeño slices. Here’s a hot tip: make sure to keep your burner on low during the cooking process to ensure an even browning and magnificently melty interior without scorching your bread.
blocks.title: Sweet & Spicy Pimento Grilled Cheese

Ah, aquafaba — a.k.a. the thick, starchy liquid you’ll find inside a can of garbanzo beans. Most people discard the stuff, but as many a vegan chef will tell you, it acts as an impressive alternative for egg whites, suitable for use in everything from baked goods to cocktails. (Aquafaba whiskey sour, anyone?) And with the addition of a stand mixer, aquafaba whips up wondrously, making it an ideal base for… Vegan Meringues!

Meringues are rather famously egg-based, so a vegan meringue might seem like a mini-miracle. But trust us, seeing (and tasting) is believing. Follow along, and we’ll show you how to turn a can of Trader Joe’s Organic Garbanzo Beans—or rather, the remnants thereof—into light, delicately crisp, coffee and matcha-flavored meringues. (Flavors imparted by none other than our 100% Colombian Instant Coffee and Matcha Green Tea sticks!) They’re simply #aquafabulous!

blocks.description: Aquafaba is the liquid found in cans of Trader Joe’s Organic Garbanzo Beans. Although often discarded, it acts as an impressive alternative for egg whites, ideal for vegan recipes. With the assistance of a stand mixer, aquafaba whips wondrously to produce egg-free meringue cookies. Take note of the measurements used to flavor the meringues, though—while the amounts may seem insignificant, we’ve allowed for just enough to impart some delightful coffee flavor, without weighing down the delicate meringues.
blocks.title: Vegan Coffee Meringues

The gifting of chocolate is a time-honored ritual come February 14th. (Let the record show that we approve of gifting chocolate anytime, but alas, we digress). Whether the recipient is your sweetie, your pals, or yourself, you can show them a choco-lot of love by way of a choc-uterie board—aka a charcuterie board that, instead of savory meats & cheeses, is laden with an abundant array of chocolatey treats in all shapes & sizes!

But how does one build a choc-uterie board? Thankfully, there’s no need to consult a diviner to solve this delicious debacle. Follow the video & guide below, then journey to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s, where you’ll find a curated collection of chocolate & candy elements sure to melt anyone’s heart.

blocks.title: How to Build a Choc-uterie Board

blocks.html: Start with a clean, dry wood serving board, appropriately sized to the number of servings and ingredients on the menu. Anchor the board with two or three of your favorite chocolates—use these categories to inspire a variety of flavors and textures:

Our customers adore dark chocolate. They also happen to be smitten with strawberries. It only seemed natural, then, to couple these favored flavors in a Cupid-worthy, limited edition Trader Joe’s Dark Chocolate Strawberry Bar ($2.99 for 3 oz.).

A velvety base of dark chocolate made with 58% cacao encases a lusciously sweet filling of strawberry juice concentrate, strawberry powder, and natural strawberry flavor. The back of the bar is adorned with pieces of freeze-dried strawberries, ensuring maximum strawberry essence, and providing a slightly crunchy counterpoint to each bite of smooth dark chocolate. Swoon.

Our Premium Milk & Dark Chocolate Almonds ($5.99 for 16 oz.) begin with dry-roasted, California-grown almonds and are finished, by hand, in small batches, using chocolate produced from a proprietary blend of cocoa beans from around the world.

Our supplier drenches about half of the almonds in sweet & creamy milk chocolate, and the other half are bathed in rich & luxurious dark chocolate. The best of both worlds in one tub? All signs point to yes.

Grahams are great. Dark Chocolate is divine. Sea Salt is splendid. But what happens when you combine all three? Well, Honey, you’re in for a treat—because when you combine all three, you get a crunchy, chocolaty, sweet n’ salty treat that we like to call Trader Joe’s Dark Chocolate Covered Honey Grahams with Sea Salt ($3.99 for 8 oz.).

While they’re remarkably resplendent eaten right out of the bag, deliver the sweet-salty effect in spades by dipping these Dark Chocolate Covered Honey Grahams into TJ’s Creamy Salted Peanut Butter.

Once you’ve drawn your selection of the major players, it’s time to fill in the spread with some minor (but no less complementary) candy couplings. Feel free to use your imagination, or turn to these taster-approved pairs:

When pairing wine with a choc-uterie board, fill your cups with one or two wines that can stand up to the myriad sweets on display, such as a lightly bubbly Giardino Pinot Grigio Vivace Rosé, or the beautifully balanced Trader Joe’s Reserve Merlot Sonoma Valley:
Finally, festoon your choc-uterie board with TJ’s fresh flowers for a fancy finishing touch!

blocks.html: When sunny weather calls and the summer breeze is a-blowin’, the last thing you want is to be stuck inside at the stove. Thankfully, Trader Joe’s stocks an abundance of supplies to support simple yet satisfying meal prep in the great outdoors. Peep the videos and check out the accompanying recipes—a full day’s menu adaptable to adventuring in the wilderness or grilling on the patio—then stop by your neighborhood store to gear up for fireside feasting!

Skip the protein bar and start your day with this satisfying, veggie-packed hash. It leans on Trader Joe’s Greek Chickpeas with Parsley & Cumin to deliver protein and a plethora of flavors thanks to its namesake ingredients (as well as the included garlic, black pepper, and lemon juice), and it utilizes the oil in the can to cook the entire dish. Rise and shine, indeed!

blocks.description:
Inside each humble can of Trader Joe’s Greek Chickpeas with Parsley & Cumin you’ll find cooked chickpeas in soybean oil and lemon juice, seasoned with parsley, salt, cumin, garlic powder, and black pepper—that’s it! All dressed up and ready to eat, they’re as terrific a dinnertime side dish as they are eaten straight out of the can for an on-the-go lunch. You can even use them in this outdoor-friendly breakfast hash recipe that uses the seasoned oil in the can to cook the entire dish!

Pro-tip: Skip the on-site prep by slicing the peppers and onion ahead of time, packing in reusable containers, and storing in the cooler until it’s time to cook.
blocks.title: Veggie Chickpea Hash

blocks.html: This recipe catapults the classic flavors of an AB&J sandwich squarely into dessert territory. Generous dollops of nutty Salted Almond Butter and sweet-tart Organic Raspberry Preserves satiate both sweet and salty cravings, while the melted Dark Chocolate Bark with Almond, Pretzel, & Sea Salt provides a toothsome crunch against the backdrop of warm banana. Bonus: you’ll cut down on dishes by using the banana peel to cook and serve!

blocks.description:
Some things in this world are all bark and no bite. Trader Joe’s Dark Chocolate Bark with Almond, Pretzel, & Sea Salt, on the other hand, is all bark and just begging for a bite! Each bag contains super snackable pieces of rich dark chocolate, studded with crunchy roasted almond and pretzel pieces and topped with a sufficient sprinkling of sea salt.

Packed in a resealable bag that makes it a particularly swell on-the-go snack or sweet treat on its own, it elevates customary camping desserts like s’mores or these Almond Butter and Raspberry Preserve-drizzled Banana Boats with ease!
blocks.title: AB&J Banana Bark Boats

blocks.html: If you’ll be cooking away from home, a little pre-adventure prep goes a long way. Slice the peppers and onions for the recipes and store them in the cooler, and prep a batch of Trailblazer Bites to fuel your outdoor fun between meals!

blocks.description: Searching for a snack-on-the-go that will fuel your figurative furnace and satiate your sweet tooth, all at the same time? Look no further than these date & TJ's Raw Almond-based bites, amped up with savory almond butter, hearty oats & flax, and semi-sweet chocolate chips.

Whether you think of it as a balm for the soul, the cure for what ails you, or simply a go-to weeknight meal option, there’s nothing like a hearty bowl of chicken soup to warm you up, both literally and figuratively, as cooler temps creep in. And whether the vibe is “Pour, stir, eat” or “Chef level: Expert,” you can find what you need to brew up a belly-warming, soul-reviving bowl of chicken soup at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s.

Below, you’ll find two recipes straight from the TJ’s test kitchen that rely on classic Trader Joe’s products—in deliciously unexpected ways—to satisfy chicken soup cravings. In summary, soup’s on!

Cooking a fantastic soup need not be an hours-long affair of simmering and stirring. In fact, this recipe for Quick Chicken Tortilla Soup can be ready to enjoy in about 15 minutes! It relies on a few pantry essentials that you can keep on hand whenever the hankering for a hearty soup strikes, and it’s anchored by none other than Trader Joe’s Salsa Autentica.

A customer favorite in our salsa set for 30 years and counting, this Salsa’s tangy tomato base is punctuated with yellow chili pepper, salt, and vinegar, along with notes of onion and garlic, lending it a crowd-pleasing, medium spicy profile ideal for topping tacos, bolstering burritos, elevating scrambled eggs—and of course, spiking a simple soup with savory heat. Set this soup a-simmering while you chop up avocado, cilantro, fresh limes, and tortilla chips, and dinner is served!

blocks.description: With its simple, wholesome ingredients and medium-spicy flavor profile, Trader Joe’s Salsa Autentica is a natural addition to any meat or plant-based tacos, and an excellent sidekick for chip dipping—but did you know it makes a super soup starter, too? Use it in this recipe that relies on a few pantry favorites to get dinner on the table in under 15 minutes.
blocks.title: Quick Chicken Tortilla Soup

blocks.html: Feeling the pull of heartier fare? Look no further than this recipe for Chicken & Dumplings Soup. TJ’s BBQ Teriyaki Chicken (yes, from our freezers!) is simmered with Trader Joe’s Organic Free Range Chicken Broth to create the soup’s unctuous base. Its velvety texture is further fortified by quartered TJ’s Organic Biscuits that have been tossed in flour.

This time-saving trifecta turns what would normally be an all-afternoon task into a ready-in-30-minutes, weeknight friendly riff on a comfort food classic. 

Made for us from organically raised chickens and organic vegetables like celery, onions, and carrots, TJ’s Organic Free Range Chicken Broth adds terrific flavor to basics like mashed potatoes or rice, and makes great bases for sauces, gravies, and of course, soups! It's also gluten free (believe it or not, some broths have added gluten). Keep a container or two handy for a flavor boost that’s as easy as “open and pour.”

blocks.description:
Boost your soups, stews, and sauces with rich, simmered-for-hours flavor—minus the simmered-for-hours work—with Trader Joe’s Organic Free Range Chicken Broth. Combined with TJ’s BBQ Teriyaki Chicken and TJ’s Organic Biscuits, they are the time-saving trifecta that makes this cozy Chicken & Dumplings Soup ready to serve in 30 minutes!

Note: For a lighter, equally satisfying soup, skip the cream. Craving a little more comfort? Double the amount.
blocks.title: Chicken & Dumplings Soup

With leaves falling and temps cooling, ‘tis the season for rich ’n cozy eats—and frankly, there are few fall dishes that a bit of butter wouldn’t better! In this recipe video, we’re showing you how to whip up not one, but two different kinds of compound butter (or “fancy flavored butter,” as it’s often called in the TJ’s test kitchen), using Trader Joe’s Unsalted Butter Quarters and just a few extra, butter-ly delightful TJ’s ingredients. 

First up, we’ll gather some organic rosemary, sage, and thyme and roll out an Herby Compound Butter so fragrant, it’ll make your turkey, mashed potatoes, and roasted veggies sing. Then, we’ll craft a Crunchy Chili Onion Butter that’ll bring the heat to any meal—whether that’s an all-out Thanksgiving feast or a simple, Tuesday-night pasta dinner.

What's more, these recipes can be prepped in advance to ease your to-do list, and will ensure an even tastier end result—a culinary compounding of interest, if you will.  Let’s get churning, er, mixing...

Holidays aside, our Unsalted Butter Quarters and Salted Butter Quarters are the building blocks of so many magnificent meals & decadent desserts. Each one-pound package contains four, four-ounce quarters made from pasteurized, Grade AA cream—the highest grade available—from cows never treated with rBST. Whether you choose to bolster your butter with tasty inclusions, or put it to work as-is, TJ’s Butter Quarters offer up a creamy, full-flavored value that can’t be beat!

blocks.description:
Trader Joe’s Unsalted Butter Quarters is a suberb choice for spreading over toast, adorning a bowl of mashed potatoes, and basting your holiday TJ's All-Natural Turkey. Butter yet, bolster a stick of Unsalted Butter with fresh herbs and seasoning to make an aromatic compound butter. Tuck a few slices under the skin of your bird before roasting, and use the rest to baste during cooking, infusing the classic aromas of Thanksgiving into every bite.

Pro-tip: Prepare the compound butter up to one week in advance. Once it's been prepped, stick it in the fridge to firm up, then it's ready whenever you need it!
blocks.title: Herby Compound Butter

blocks.description:
Made from a smoky, savory mixture of crunchy garlic, onion, peppers and olive oil, Trader Joe’s Crunchy Chili Onion ranks high in the “great on everything” hall of fame. It's equally great when combined with TJ's Unsalted Butter to make this easy yet impressive compound butter that adds a whole lot of complexity to an array of dishes. Spread it over TJ's Dinner Rolls, add a pat to mashed potatoes, and use it to flavor and baste your TJ's All-Natural Turkey for Thanksgiving! 

Pro-tip: Prepare the compound butter up to one week in advance. Once it's been prepped, stick it in the fridge to firm up, then it's ready whenever you need it!

Frankly speaking, there are few fall dishes that a bit of butter wouldn’t better. On second thought, there are few dishes, period, that a bit of butter wouldn’t better! And while butter by itself is a boon to anything it touches, butter all dressed up in spices, seasonings, and/or sweet ‘n savory inclusions—a.k.a. Compound Butter—is even better.

Consider, for example, the transformative power of Trader Joe’s Butter with Parmesan, Garlic & Herb. Made for us in small batches by a creamery with an uncommon knack for fancy, flavored butters, each four-ounce roll contains roughly 25% Parmesan cheese by weight, plus shallots, dried garlic, salt, and parsley; it lends rich, full flavor to everything from scrambled eggs and toasted baguettes to seared steaks and baked potatoes.

Feeling culinarily creative? You can also make your own Compound Butters, using Trader Joe’s Unsalted Butter Quarters as your base and a few extra, butterly delightful TJ’s ingredients of your choosing...

If it’s heat that you seek, a tablespoon or two (or three!) of Trader Joe’s Crunchy Chili Onion is just the ticket to creating a Compound Butter that brings savory, spicy chili-onion flavor to any meal—whether that’s a Tuesday-night pasta dinner or an all-out fall feast.

It's equally great when combined with TJ's Unsalted Butter to make this easy yet impressive compound butter that adds a whole lot of complexity to an array of dishes. Spread it over TJ's Dinner Rolls, add a pat to mashed potatoes, and use it to flavor and baste your TJ's All-Natural Turkey for Thanksgiving! 

Pro-tip: Prepare the compound butter up to one week in advance. Once it's been prepped, stick it in the fridge to firm up, then it's ready whenever you need it!

When there’s a chill in the air and you find yourself in need of warming up, we find that one of the coziest, comfiest, and tastiest ways to do so is by simmering a pot of congee on the stove. A traditional dish that goes back quite literally thousands of years in China (where it’s known as zhōu in Mandarin, or jūk in Cantonese), congee is a mild and savory rice porridge that’s spectacularly suited to accessorizing with alliums and aromatics, and takes well to topping with veggies and proteins of all kinds.

In the following video, we’ve assembled some step-by-step instructions for a hearty, homey Miso Congee with Honey-Miso Squash, starring Trader Joe's White Miso Paste, ideal for serving on a blustery, wintry weekend. Visit your neighborhood Trader Joe’s, grab the ingredients, and try the recipe out for yourself: a warming, welcoming, anytime dish awaits you!

blocks.title: Miso Congee with Honey Miso Squash

blocks.html: Because its base of rice and water is so sublimely simple (and easy to adjust, as far as consistency goes), congee easily acts as a jumping-off point for all sorts of kitchen-warming, crowd-pleasing flavor combos, from spicy chili paste, to umami-rich Miso, to zesty ginger, and beyond.

Sometimes congee is served with briny pickles for breakfast, sometimes with sweet red bean paste for dessert, sometimes with seafood filets or silky-textured chicken breast for dinner (—sometimes, it’s even served cold, to cool down on a hot day). However and whenever it’s served, though, congee is certain to satisfy.

Customize this capable congee recipe with a few TJ’s favorites (a handful of Fried Shallots, a drizzle of Crunchy Sesame Sunflower Seeds Pepitas Salsa Macha, a sprinke of fresh Green Onions), or feel free to experiment to fit your culinary preferences.

blocks.description:
Trader Joe’s White Miso Paste is made of fermented rice and soybeans, and like many fantastic, fermented foods, it has a complex flavor—a mix of savory, salty, and umami. Our White Miso Paste is made with a shorter-than-standard fermentation period to yield a delicate umami flavor, making this a very versatile Miso. It plays dual roles in this cozy, highly customizable congee dish—flavoring the rice porridge base and adding oomph to the roasted squash topping.

Customize Your Congee: Walk the aisles of your neighborhood Trader Joe’s and you will find an array of crunchy, spicy, herby, and umami-packed products that make superb congee toppings and will enhance your congee-eating experience. Choose what you like, skip what you don't! If you need some suggestions, we recommend a sprinkle of Roasted & Salted Pumpkin Seeds, a generous drizzle of Crunchy Sesame Sunflower Pepita Salsa Macha, a touch of fresh Green Onions, and a handful of Fried Shallots, to name a few. But as we said, you do you!

blocks.html: Undisputed champions of the cutest culinary couple award, wine & dessert pairings offer a decadence that wine and cheese just can’t quite touch (no offense meant to our favorite fromages, of course). To prove the aforementioned asseveration, we’ve put together a sip-erb assembly of wine and dessert twosomes that spans varietals and flavor profiles, peak pairs that are sure to please whether your dessert desires are fruity, creamy, or chocolatey. Try our suggested pairings below, or come up with your own cuvée & cupcake couplets. After all, where there’s a wine, there’s a way—and where there’s a neighborhood Trader Joe’s, there’s wine* and dessert (in our stores where wine is sold, of course). Cheers!

A semi-dry sparkler with essence of yellow apple and ripe apricot, Schloss Biebrich Sekt ($6.99* for 750mL) says “fancy” for an almost-too-good-to-be true price—big reasons that make it a customer favorite for brunches, wedding receptions, and baby showers. Its fruit-forward profile and fantastic fizz are ideal foils for the soft, creamy lemon layer nestled atop the dense, deliciously crumbly shortbread base in each box of Trader Joe’s Classic Lemon Bars ($4.49 for 10.6 ounces). Simply defrost at room temperature for an hour before serving and you’ll have a fancy, tart, bite-sized sweet that stands up to the bubbly Sekt.

Coming to us from Paso Robles, California, Corvelia Cabernet Sauvignon ($9.99* for 750mL) is a strong and structured red, replete with notes of currant, blackberry, dark cherry, and tobacco. An oak influence lends this TJ’s exclusive some serious backbone. Its boldness begs for a baked good with a bit of bravado, like Trader Joe’s Chocolate Brooklyn Babka. Our beloved Babka ($4.99 for 18 ounces) is made for us in—where else?—Brooklyn, New York by a small, kosher bakery that began in their grandmother’s kitchen, so when we say this is basically your bubbe’s Babka, we mean it. The supplier spreads the sweet, yeasty, scratch-made dough with a rich, chocolate filling, then twists it by hand and places it in a high loaf pan to be proofed and baked. Sliced and served warm, it really is a compelling Cab companion—pop a bottle and fuhgeddaboudit!

In answer to the above, well, we think you’d be wise to stay. Why? Because we’re having a party, and you’re invited! We’re setting a celebratory tone with a bottle of Big Churn Chardonnay ($6.99* for 750mL). With its superbly rich finish and luxurious body, it’s an oaky-buttery, only-at-TJ’s white that’s best with a super-sweet-yet simple treat—like Trader Joe’s Mini Cupcakes ($3.99 for 12 ounces). Each package contains twelve, too-cute, two-bite, tender-crumbed cupcakes; six vanilla with vanilla buttercream frosting and six chocolate with chocolate buttercream. Buttery begets buttery, right? And did we mention they're gluten free*?!

blocks.html: Semifreddo (Italian for “half frozen”) is a light & refreshing Italian dessert with a texture that lies somewhere between ice cream and mousse. It’s often filled with rich sauces, ripe fruit, and chopped nuts to complement the lusciously creamy mouthfeel, and since you can freeze it in a loaf pan to enjoy later, it’s an excellent, no-bake dessert option for when it’s too hot to turn on the oven.

Our PB&J Semifreddo recipe takes a delicious detour from the traditional egg yolk base of the classic dessert—making it a semi-semifreddo, if you will—instead calling on mascarpone, heavy whipping cream, and smooth peanut butter to create its craveably creamy texture. (With a classic PB&J on our minds, we’ve included Freeze Dried Strawberries and strawberry preserves to add a nostalgic angle to this timely twist on tradition.)

Pick up the ingredients at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s, then watch the video for step-by-step instructions to steer you toward sweet, semifreddo satisfaction.

With a multitude of noodle shapes & sizes—and so many ways to make, serve, and enjoy them—our pasta is the proverbial blank canvas you need to create delicious dinners on the fly.

Check out these recipes for timesaving shortcuts, inspired swap-ins, and terrifically tasty hacks. Everything for a primo pasta dinner tonight is just a quick trip to your neighborhood TJ's away...

It’s tough to beat a bowl of buttered noodles—their cozy, mellow flavor shines with savory simplicity, while at the same time serving as an adept partner to an array of seasonings and sauce boosters, like Trader Joe’s Gochujang Paste. Gochujang offers a beautiful balance of sweet and heat that, when combined with salted butter and a few pantry staples, creates a pasta sauce that’s simultaneously complex and comforting as it envelops every edge of Trader Joe’s Organic Spaghetti alla Chitarra Pasta (these unique noodles are square, not round—neat!). For even more aromatic oomph, might we suggest chopped TJ’s Garlic? The number of cloves in the recipe is just a suggestion…

blocks.description:
Quite pasta-bly the most famous noodle in the world, spaghetti is made a bit differently in the Italian region of Abruzzo, just east of Rome. Just like standard spaghetti, the Abruzzese version is long and thin, made with durum wheat semolina and water, but instead of having a rounded shape, this spaghetti is uniquely square and goes by the name spaghetti alla chitarra. Cooked to al dente, Trader Joe’s Spaghetti alla Chitarra’s shape and toothsome texture are well-suited to the buttery, spicy notes of the Gochujang Paste-infused sauce in this recipe.

Note: Before draining your cooked spaghetti, reserve a cup of the starchy pasta water to help emulsify the sauce. Add it little by little to the pan until your gochujang sauce becomes smooth, shiny, and thoroughly coats every noodle.
blocks.title: Garlicky Gochujang Spaghetti

blocks.html:

The recipe calls for ready-to-heat-and-eat ingredients like grocery aisle superstar Trader Joe’s Roasted Garlic Marinara Sauce, and your favorite TJ’s refrigerated ravioli that cook directly in the sauce, to save prep time and cut down on dishes. Win-win!

In addition to upgrading a classic penne or spaghetti, it adds serious oomph layered in lasagna or a homemade chicken parmesan. You could choose which one to try first, or you can combine them into one epic pasta bake! This four-ingredient recipe requires only three steps—assemble, bake, eat!

Habanero peppers range between 100,000 and 350,000 in Scoville heat units (the scale that measures the spiciness of chili peppers)—meaning habaneros certainly bring the heat! When life gets turned upside down, it’s generally regarded as a not-so-great thing. But in the context of cake, upside-down is actually a desirable state of being. There’s the drama of the pan flip and reveal, the glamour of the caramelized crust laden with sweet fruit… an upside-down cake delivers delight in every forkful.

If the thought of flipping a hot cake pan has you running for the hills, fear not: this Olive Oil & Citrus Upside-Down Cake recipe is TJ’s test kitchen-tested and taster-approved—and more importantly, it reliably results in a crowd-pleasing dessert!

Visit your neighborhood Trader Joe’s to pick up the requisite Organic Spanish Extra Virgin Olive Oil (a must for achieving the cake’s signature flavor and richness) and sunshine-y citrus fruit from our fresh produce section—all at prices that will leave your budget right-side up.

Trader Joe’s is a limited assortment store, meaning we don’t offer 24 varieties of ketchup or a wall-full of mayonnaise. We tend to make exceptions to the whole “limited assortment” thing, though, when it comes to olive oil. There’s just so much remarkably flavorful olive oil being produced all over the world, from Italy to California, to Tunisia, to Spain…

Speaking of Spain, the country is a veritable treasure trove of olive groves; its rolling hills are home to some of the world’s most flavorful olives, including the Picual, Picuda, and Arbequino varieties used in our Extra Virgin Olive Oil from Spain. This blend of olives produces oil that’s light green in color and a bit fruity, with a refreshing verdant flavor.
Use it in dressings or marinades, or for dipping your favorite crusty bread... and of course, in cake!

blocks.description:

Ah, gnocchi. Those petite Italian dumplings have become a powerhouse in the Trader Joe’s freezers over the years. What began as an easy way to enjoy Italian-style restaurant favorites in your home (at a fraction of the cost, we might add) has blossomed into a category in its own right, replete with tasty renditions of the classics, as well as vegetable-based offerings that satiate carb cravings with a lower caloric impact—while still tasting fantastic!

Here we’ve created a guide to pairing Trader Joe’s Gnocchi knockouts with the ubiquitous line of Charles Shaw Wines. Why Charles Shaw, you may ask? It’s simple. They’ve proven—consistently, for close to two decades—wine doesn’t need to be expensive to be good, drinkable, and enjoyable. And we know for sure you won’t find wine this enjoyable at such a gnoc-your-socks-off value anywhere other than your neighborhood Trader Joe’s.

Northern Italy lays claim to the invention of gnocchi, the pillowy potato dumplings coveted for their cozy bite, and Gorgonzola, the beloved, soft, blue-veined cheese with nutty aroma. Trader Joe’s lays claim to Gnocchi al Gorgonzola (16 ounces for $3.49), which marries these beautiful creations to make an inviting, delicious dish. Come to think of it, we also lay claim to Charles Shaw Cabernet Sauvignon (750mL for $3.99*)—a deep, ruby-colored wine with aromatics of blackberry and vanilla, that happens to be a natural fit for rich, cheesy pasta.

As we’ve said before, any way is a good way to dress up Trader Joe’s Cauliflower Gnocchi (12 ounces for $3.29). Balance the flavors of earthy butternut squash, green peas, and zesty, ginger-forward yellow curry sauce in this recipe with the tropical notes and clean finish found in a glass of chilled Charles Shaw Pinot Grigio (750mL for $3.99*).

When you consume coffee for pleasure, we say you’re “drinking” it. But, when you consume coffee with the specific goal of tasting it deeply, assessing its character, and rating its qualities—we say you’re “cupping” it. 

We went to visit some cupping experts (called “cuppers,” of course!), and they showed us firsthand how Trader Joe’s coffees are cupped each time a batch of beans is freshly roasted...

In this example of coffee cupping, the same roast is tasted against itself to ensure consistent quality. Ground beans are precisely measured in identical cups and brewed using the steeping method for the most authentic flavor. Cuppers smell the coffee every step of the process.

After brewing, cuppers remove the “crust” of grounds from the top of each cup and rinse the spoons in between, and then loudly slurp the coffee from the spoon to spray it into their mouth for maximum tasting. Finally, approved roasts are packaged and sent to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s, where you can buy them and taste them, too!

  • Don’t be afraid to char your ingredients! The grill marks will add a sweet complexity because of the sugar contentin both the pineapple and the Soyaki glaze.

Soyaki has been a staple in our grocery aisle for 20 years—and for good reason. Aromatic garlic, zesty ginger, and preservative-free soy sauce form the sauce’s irresistible, sweet-savory base, while sesame seeds add a mild, nutty profile and pleasing texture.

In this recipe, it gives the chops a complex and lively profile of bright, salty, and sweet notes, achieved through a marinade and glazing technique, creating a true taste sensation.

As a marinade for just about for any grilled protein or veg, Soyaki provides maximum flavor with minimal effort. No grill? No problem. It’s a dream for broiling or baking, you can use it as a stir-fry sauce, or even as a dipping sauce for our impressive selection of dumplings!

You know what they say—you can’t go wrong with a warm, fresh-from-the-fryer jelly donut. (Surely, somebody has said that... and if not, we just did.) This is true any time of year, but with a chill in the air and the holidays fast approaching, now is an especially excellent time to indulge in this comforting classic.  

While variations of these doughy, deep-fried delights emerged during Hanukkah celebrations throughout history (with about as many names), Israel’s sufganiyot (pronounced “soof-gahn-eeyot”) were especially championed as a Hanukkah treat. And now, you can enjoy these pillowy, stuffed-with-Strawberry Preserves donuts in your home kitchen, thanks to this easy-peasy sufganiyot recipe video and a trip to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s—no donut pans or deep-fryers needed!

Simply follow along with our video, then head to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s to gather your ingredients. And if jelly isn’t your jam, you're still in luck—you can fill these beignet-like beauties with just about anything your heart desires, from Cocoa Almond Spread to Lemon Curd to Cookie Butter and beyond!

While it is, of course, the jelly that puts the “jelly” in “jelly donut” (literally and figuratively), donut overlook the importance of Trader Joe’s Organic Powdered Cane Sugar in this recipe.

For those unfamiliar, powdered sugar is simply sugar that’s been blitzed to form a fine, soft powder. Here, it’s pulling double-duty by sweetening the batter and delicately decorating the donuts!

Fun fact: TJ’s Organic Powdered Sugar is made with organically grown cane sugar and tapioca starch to act as an anti-clumping agent, yet our price is on par with brands that use conventionally grown (non-organic) sugar and corn starch. Pretty sweet, right?

blocks.description:
These Sufganiyot, or fried donuts, make a fun, customizable, downright delicious baking project that can be made from flour to finish in under three hours (and that includes two hours of hands-off proofing time!)

The dough is lightly sweetened with Trader Joe's Organic Powdered Cane Sugar and the finished donuts are served with a snow-like sprinkle to complement an array of fillings, from classic Strawberry Preserves or Raspberry Preserves to TJ's Lemon Curd, or Cocoa Almond Spread. Choose your favorite or fry them all—your donuts, your choice!  

Pro-tip: Use an instant-read thermometer to check the oil temperature between batches. When dough is added, it can quickly lower the temperature. Make sure the oil returns to 325°F before adding more dough to ensure evenly cooked donuts.

Inspired by the ancient English Yuletide tradition from which it takes its name, Trader Joe’s Winter Wassail Punch is a festive blend of apple, cherry, black currant, and lemon juices, infused with orange peel, cinnamon, nutmeg, clove, cardamom, and ginger. With strong notes of clove, cinnamon, and various herbs, Trader Joe’s Classic Bitters are delightfully aromatic and spice-forward, adding depth and nuance to... anything. And we’re not just talking drinks—you can sprinkle bitters on ice cream and even add them to marinades.

Point of order: like most bitters, our Classic Bitters do contain alcohol. But because bitters are measured by the dash (think drops, not pours), they're excellent for adding interest to an otherwise ordinary beverage, with a nearly nonalcoholic outcome. blocks.html: Interested in turning over a new leaf when it comes to answering the eternal question of “What’s for dinner?” Have you resolved to up your cooking game, or simply reduce your number of trips to the drive-thru? Whatever your intention, you’re in luck! Trader Joe’s offers a curated collection of fresh produce, pantry essentials, and plenty more to add excitement to meal prep and help achieve your dinner goals—all at incredible prices. Case in point: Trader Joe’s Organic Coconut Aminos Seasoning Sauce, featured in this weeknight-winning recipe video for Seared Salmon & Quick-Pickled Cucumbers.

Made in Sri Lanka, this Organic Coconut Aminos Seasoning Sauce starts with organic coconut sap that’s been hand-harvested and fermented, then boiled and seasoned with sea salt to create an amino-rich sauce with a whole host of uses. Flavor-wise, coconut does not come to mind: Organic Coconut Aminos can be likened to soy sauce, though not quite as salty, and with a touch of sweetness. There are no soy ingredients in this product, and at 200mg of sodium per tablespoon (vs. 920mg in the leading soy sauce brand), this gluten-free, kosher (pareve) Sauce is a great option for those looking to reduce their sodium intake.

The savory notes of Organic Coconut Aminos Seasoning Sauce offer mouthwatering depth of flavor to the aforementioned seared salmon, further complemented by fresh, herby dill and aromatic garlic. You can also use the Sauce as a seasoning springboard in a freestyled fried rice, or to add complexity to sautéed veggies and soups. Or splash it into to salad dressing or a spicy Bloody Mary for extra umami. Or… you get the idea.

blocks.description:
This seared salmon gets its savory, complex flavor from a 30-minute rest in an Organic Coconut Aminos Seasoning Sauce-infused marinade—which also serves as the base of a lemony, glossy finishing sauce for serving the fish. While the salmon marinates, you can whip up a batch of quick-pickled cucumbers, enjoy an evening walk, or kick back and relax until it’s time to fire up the burner.

Pro-tip: the finishing sauce comes together very quickly—be sure to have the finishing sauce ingredients measured and ready to go before you cook the salmon.
blocks.title: Seared Salmon & Quick-Pickled Cucumbers

You’ll find Organic Coconut Aminos Seasoning Sauce on our grocery shelves, every day.

blocks.html: If you are a big fan of umami, like we are, you’re in good company—Trader Joe’s Mushroom & Company, to be precise. Made with a base of powdered porcini and white button mushrooms, along with kosher salt, onion, mustard seed, red pepper, and thyme, this magnificently Multipurpose Umami Seasoning Blend might just be one of the most versatile spices to ever appear on our shelves. In fact, we find that it’s often the only spice you’ll need to make superbly savory, marvelously umami-rich dishes of all kinds.

In this video, we’ve put that theory to test with three recipes, each a One Seasoning Wonder: lovely, multi-layered Polenta & Veggie Stacks; satisfyingly snackable Umami Parm Popcorn; and a hearty and homey Roasted Pork Tenderloin & Potatoes with Honey Umami Butter. Each one showcases Mushroom & Company’s capabilities as a one-spice-fits-all solution in the kitchen. After you’ve watched, be sure to stop by your neighborhood Trader Joe’s to see what this uniquely utile Umami Seasoning can do for you!

blocks.description:

While you can serve each ingredient next to each other, try stacking this side dish instead! TJ’s Organic Polenta makes a sturdy base for piling on all the veggies and TJ’s Silver Goat Cheese rounds. 

Almost as compelling as this recipe’s cozy deliciousness? Its sheet pan prep won’t leave you with a sink full of dishes. Hooray!

Yummmmm!

blocks.html: Cool & creamy with plenty of textural interest, potato salad is a summer comfort food classic, a captivating counterpoint to the savory meats, grilled veggies, and fresh fruit you might find on a buffet table when the weather warms up. And if warming things up piques your palate, this spicy twist on a classic potato salad recipe is a surefire way to turn up the heat, thanks to the addition of Trader Joe’s Peri-Peri Sauce.

Made for us in South Africa, where peri-peri peppers are plentiful, this curiously complex Sauce combines the welcoming heat of fermented chilies and dried chili flakes, the tangy tartness of lemon juice, and the savory splendor of garlic to create a uniquely enchanting flavor profile that goes with… almost everything.

In addition to perking up the prototypical potato salad, it can pump up grilled proteins, add verve to roasted veggies, or zhush up fish tacos. That said, drizzling with abandon is an acceptable—nay, highly recommended—serving suggestion.

If you’re looking to elevate potato salad—or fried rice, tacos, nuggets, scrambled eggs, or even hummus—to new heights this summer, head to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s and pick up a bottle of Peri-Peri Sauce—you’ll be glad you did!

blocks.description:
A little spicy, a little sour, even a little sweet, Trader Joe’s Peri-Peri Sauce contributes a whole new point of view to prototypical potato salad. Its smooth, creamy consistency and welcoming heat meld masterfully into the dressing base; combined with tender Dutch Yellow Potatoes, sliced celery, and brightly colored bell peppers, the finished dish is topped with a handful of chips for an unexpected dose of craveable crunch.

This potato salad is best served at room temperature within two hours of cooking. Store leftovers in the refrigerator and enjoy within two days.
blocks.title: Peri-Peri Potato Salad

When life gets busy (and let’s be honest, when doesn’t it?), making meals shouldn’t feel like solving an algebraic equation. Enter: Trader Joe’s Complete Salad Kits and our awesome array of ready-to-eat and pre-cooked proteins—trust us, this is the ultimate one + one = done solution!

Each one of our bagged Salad Kits already comes with what you need to toss up a tasty and Complete Salad... and when you add a protein to the mix, well, then you’ve got dinner! Or lunch. Or a side salad worthy of even the most premium potluck. Now, put THAT in a bowl and eat it. Literally.

A relative newcomer to our produce section, TJ’s Pizza Ranch Salad Kit contains a base of shredded Romaine, red cabbage, and carrots, plus packets of pizza-esque toppings like herby flatbread strips, crispy four-cheese crumbles, and grated Parmesan. 

True to its name, each Pizza Ranch Salad Kit also contains a creamy, tangy, tomato-based-pizza-sauce-meets-Ranch dressing to tie it all together. Add some sliced TJ’s Sliced Uncured Pepperoni to mix as we’ve done here, and you’ve got nothing short of a protein-packed pizza party!

TJ’s Sweet Chili Mango Salad Kit combines the cruciferous crunch of cabbage, kale, Brussels sprouts, and radicchio with the nuttiness of roasted sunflower seeds & toasted quinoa, and the sweet, chewy fruitiness of dried mango pieces. A Sweet Chili dressing ties it all together, invoking all the tangy, spicy, tropical-tasting flavors of Thai cuisine. 

In keeping with the vegan nature of this Thai-inspired Complete Salad Kit, we recommend rounding it out with cubes of TJ’s Baked Sriracha Flavored Tofu. The garlicky Sriracha flavor of this marinated, ready-to-eat Tofu plays beautifully with the other elements of the Salad, and heat-seekers will certainly appreciate its added chili kick.

TJ’s BBQ & Black Pepper Toscano Chopped Salad Kit contains a seemingly simple assembly of ingredients, but a forkful of its unexpected umami will leave you wondering, “How did they do that?!” The answer? We did it with a base of well-chopped cabbage, carrots, broccoli, and kale, a packet of miniature cornbread croutons, and, most importantly, with our very own Black Pepper Toscano cheese. 

The final stroke of boldness comes courtesy of a sweet onion BBQ dressing, which rounds out the Salad’s existing elements and provides an excellent, BBQ backdrop for the addition of TJ’s Hardwood Smoked Pulled Chicken! This boneless, skinless, white-meat chicken has been seasoned with garlic and paprika, then smoked slow ‘n low over Hardwood logs and carefully shredded. Simply heat it in your microwave for around 3 minutes, and it’s ready to up the ante on salads, sandwiches, and much more!

Watch the video play-by-play, draft your favorites, and come hungry—thankfully, you don’t need to wait for the season to start when you’ve got a free ticket to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s, every day of the year.

Trader Joe’s Sweet Pull-Apart Aloha Rolls ($2.99* for 12 ounces) are a true utility player in our bakery lineup, and the ultimate bun upon which to build the aforementioned sliders.

Just pull them apart (they come “attached” in a 3-roll by 4-roll rectangle), split them in half, and pile on the fillings. With the recipes below and a bag of sweet, fluffy Aloha Rolls in your bullpen, you’re sure to take your next slider from single-A status all the way to the big leagues (is it baseball season yet?!).

Anything’s possible, but is anything... pasta-ble? Though we’ve prepared lotsa pasta in the TJ’s test kitchen, we’re still noodling around on that one. There is one pairing we particularly love, especially when temperatures are trending downward: hot broth & pasta—plus whatever vegetables or meats have been on your mind. 

Such souped-up pastas (or should we say pasta’d-up soups?) are the focus of this recipe feature. Even a wet noodle would have to agree, each of the recipes below are pasta-tively soup-er for their ease of assembly and slurp-erb flavor profiles.

We invite you to view the video, read the recipes, and take stock of the ingredients. Then head to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s for all your soup supplies. And if you follow our advice, we promise you’ll be enjoying a steaming bowl of delicious, pasta-fied soup very, very spoon! (We meant “soon,” but that works, too.)

Why are tortellini so comforting? Maybe it's because they sometimes resemble tiny neck pillows. In the case of Trader Joe’s Spinach Tortellini, we believe it boils down to the insides, which include Spinach (of course), plus a tortally cheesy blend of ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan.

Speaking of boiling, since this pasta is “fresh” (not dried), it reaches tender taste-ability very quickly. Drop the Tortellini in the immersion-blended chicken broth and veggie base just a few minutes before serving, and you’ll have a truly cozy bowl to share. (Garnish with fresh parsley and more Parmesan. Not recommended for bumpy airplane rides.)

blocks.description:
Trader Joe's Spinach Tortellini are like little pasta pockets stuffed with a flavorful mix of spinach, ricotta, mozzarella and Parmesan. And because they are fresh, not dried, they cook in 2-3 minutes. Yes!

Our Spinach Tortellini are spectacular in soups—brothy or creamy—and this recipe is a little bit of both. By blending the cooked vegetables with the heated broth, the result is thicker than your typical broth-based soup, without the addition of any cream.

Pro-tip: Save your Parmesan rinds! After you’ve grated the very last bit of your favorite Trader Joe’s Parmesan block, you can use the rind to enhance soups and sauces. If you won’t be cooking with it right away, seal it and freeze until needed.

As-is, it’s quick, convenient, and delicious, but if you have more time, it’s not hard to notch up these noodles once more with a soft-boiled egg, quick-simmered Shiitakes, some fresh green veggies, and a few flecks of Furikake. It’ll be worth the “work,” when the pay-off is a Ramen cup that overfloweth with true noodle-shop vibes.

blocks.description:
Trader Joe’s Miso Ramen Soup is not your typical instant ramen cup. Included alongside its impeccably crafted blend of seasonings is a packet of sunflower oil. Adding both to the noodles during preparation ensures not only a delightfully savory broth, rich with flavors of miso, garlic, notes of umami and seaweed, but a silky-smooth texture for your noodles—the days of dry-textured instant noodles are over!

This recipe bridges the gap between the convenience of instant ramen with the expansive flavors and aromas of a noodle shop Miso Ramen bowl, thanks to the addition of a few TJ’s products to offer an elevated eating experience with just 20 minutes of prep.

“That’s the way the cookie crumbles…” This turn of phrase is typically uttered when something doesn’t go quite the way you’d planned—but what if the cookie crumbling allows for the creation of something even sweeter in the process?

We tested this theory on Trader Joe’s Speculoos Cookies in the TJ’s Test Kitchen (it’s a rough gig, we know), and the resulting recipe is nothing short of breathtaking. Watch this Cookie Butter & Coffee Ice Cream Cake recipe video to see what looking on the bright side of crumbled cookies can do for dessert, then head to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s to make this dreamy dish a reality!

The crisp, golden-brown base layer of this ice cream cake is built upon crumbled Speculoos Cookies. (When they’re not moonlighting as ice cream cake crust, their cinnamon-y sweetness, snappy texture, and thin, oblong shape make these vegan Cookies a capital accompaniment to a hot cup of coffee or tea or an ice-cold glass of milk. Alas, we digress.)

Velvety Coffee Bean Blast Ice Cream and Speculoos Cookie Butter Ice Cream are layered atop the crust, split with a fluffy Speculoos Cookie Butter Spread-infused whipped cream that’s speckled with more crushed Speculoos Cookies throughout.

Spiked with Trader Joe’s Fleur de Sel Caramel Sauce and garnished with more whipped cream, and even more Speculoos Cookies (are you sensing a theme here?), it’s drizzled with more Caramel Sauce, culminating in an irresistible ice cream cake with sweetly epic proportions, made for serious dessert devotees.

Spring, the season of renewal, is always an excellent time for some tidying up, and that includes the contents of your fridge. Now, if you’re anything like us, in the course of fridge-tidying, you may find yourself asking questions like, “What should I do with the last little bit of mustard?” “What’s a quick way to use up this spoonful-and-a-half of strawberry jam?” “Surely there’s a better way to finish off the peanut butter without just eating it directly from the jar, right?” (The answer to that last one might surprise you!)

In the spirit of spring cleaning, we’ve rounded up some recipes to put those last little remainders of your favorite Trader Joe’s products to good use. Who knew tidying up could be so tasty?

blocks.description:
When there isn’t quite enough Trader Joe’s Aioli Garlic Mustard Sauce left to spread on a sandwich, use the rest (and the jar) to make an all-purpose salad dressing! Toss this tangy dressing with your favorite TJ’s lettuce mix, over a grain bowl, or roasted veggies to easily wake up those weeknight meals.

The more mustard sauce in the jar, the zippier it’ll be. Mixing the dressing in the jar cuts down on dishes, too. Win-win!
blocks.title: Almost-Empty Mustard-Jar Dressing

blocks.html:
Why do you still have that almost-empty jar of Trader Joe’s Aioli Garlic Mustard Sauce in your fridge? It's because this spread’s slightly spicy, not-too-pungent mustard, blended with a mellow garlic sauce, is impossibly delicious—and nearly impossible to throw out! But if there’s not enough to spread on a sandwich, you can still use what’s left to make an all-purpose salad dressing.

Toss this dressing with your favorite TJ’s lettuce mix, over a grain bowl, or roast with veggies to easily wake up those weekday meals. The more mustard sauce in the jar, the zippier it’ll be. Use the mustard jar itself to combine and emulsify the dressing to cut down on the number of dirty dishes, too. Win-win!

blocks.description: When there isn’t quite enough Trader Joe’s Organic Creamy Salted Valencia Peanut Butter left to spread on a sandwich, use the rest (and the jar) to make overnight oats! Peanut butter adds savory oomph to the oats and the jar makes a superb serving vessel for on-the-go breakfasting!
blocks.title: PB-Jar Overnight Oats

blocks.html:
Still scraping the insides of that Trader Joe’s Organic Creamy Salted Valencia Peanut Butter jar? We’re not surprised, since this PB trades typical Runner peanuts for organic Valencia peanuts—which are naturally sweet with a more intense flavor. When there isn’t quite enough for one more PB&J, we suggest repurposing the remnants to make overnight oats.

The Peanut Butter adds oodles of oomph to your oats, while the jar makes a superb serving vessel for on-the-go breakfasting!

blocks.description:
When you get to the bottom of the Trader Joe’s Strawberry Preserves jar and there isn’t quite enough to spread on toast, use the rest (and the jar) to make a cocktail! Using the jar as your cocktail shaker, combine leftover preserves with vodka and whatever herbs and citrus you have on hand for a refreshing, sensationally simple cocktail.

Have a bit more jam leftover? Double the recipe for two drinks!
blocks.title: Jam-Jar Cocktail

blocks.html:
Put freshly picked strawberries, sugar, lemon juice, and fruit pectin in a jar (carefully, of course), and you get a berritable jam-boree of sweet, fruity flavor, aka Trader Joe’s Strawberry Preserves. Of course you want to rescue every last lick from the insides of the jar, but if you're short on tiny spatulas (and your tongue is too short), try mixing a cocktail in the jar.

When the jar becomes your cocktail shaker, you can easily combine your leftover Preserves with vodka and whatever herb and citrus you have on hand to create a refreshing, sensationally simple cocktail. Still more Preserves in reserve? Double the recipe for two drinks!

Spring has officially sprung! For fastidious fans of the spick-and-span, this can only mean one thing: it’s time for some serious spring cleaning. Not much of a neatnik? No worries. Spring is the perfect time to turn over a new leaf…

Lucky for you, Trader Joe’s makes sprucing-up simple, affordable, and—dare we say—fun. (Yes, fun!) Take a peek at some our preferred perennial purification essentials, then join us for a tidy tiptoe through the tulips, a.k.a. the household products section at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s, in celebration of spring spotlessness!

Dirty dishes are a drag. With the right tools, though, they can be a stellar springboard into spring cleaning. When it comes to washing your wares, we recommend always having a bottle of TJ’s Lavender Tea Tree Scent Liquid Dish Soap or TJ’s Citrus Scent Liquid Dish Soap (each $2.99 for 25 fl. oz.) and a pack of TJ’s Pop-Up Sponges ($7.99 for a package of 12) at your disposal. Or near your disposal. Either works.

This dynamic duo is a plant-based, grease-cutting dream come true. Our Liquid Dish Soap is highly efficacious (a little goes a long way), hypoallergenic, and free from unnecessary coloring agents and phosphates. Our 100% cellulose Pop-Up Sponges come flat, spring to life in water (nifty, no?), and are known to be impressively durable. Together, they’re a biodegradable match made in household chore heaven.

TJ’s Cedarwood & Sage Multi-Purpose Cleaner delivers all the cleaning power you want, minus the harsh chemicals, dyes, and synthetic fragrances you don’t. It’s biodegradable, not tested on animals, and ready for use on any water-safe surface—like granite countertops, glass, tile, linoleum, stainless steel, and more. We’re selling each 34-oz. spray bottle for $2.99—the same great price we’ve held for almost 20 years.

Whether you’re looking at a small, weekly wash or facing loads upon loads of laundry, TJ’s Lavender Scent Liquid Laundry Detergent ($9.99 for 100 fl. oz. – about 100 loads) and TJ’s Free & Clear Liquid Laundry Detergent ($5.99 for 50 fl. oz. – about 50 loads) are ready to tackle the task. Both formulas are hypoallergenic, biodegradable, and free from dyes, optical brighteners, phthalates, and phosphates. The Free & Clear version is fragrance-free, while the Lavender version gets its subtle scent from lavender essential oil.

For an even longer-lingering lavender scent, toss a TJ’s Lavender Dryer Bag ($4.49 for a box of four) in the dryer along with those luxe linens of yours. There’s nothing like wrapping up in a lavender-scented bath towel after a warm shower or curling up in lavender-scented sheets after a stressful day. Each Dryer Bag contains just one ingredient (dried lavender) and lasts around 5-10 cycles each. Once they reach the end of their lifespan, you’ll have another use for these sachets: sprinkle the florets on your carpet and vacuum them up for an instant room-refresher!

Time for the final freshening! Most air and room fresheners contain a myriad of harsh, synthetic fragrances, which can be more like a migraine-in-the-making than a breath of fresh air. TJ’s Super Lemon Room Spritz ($1.99 for 1.69 fl. oz.) however, is made with lemon myrtle oil, spearmint oil, water, and a small amount of sorbitol-based emulsifier to keep the oil and water from separating. It all adds up to a generous bounty of citrusy cheer in one, petite-yet-powerful spray bottle.

Last bud not least: what’s bright, colorful, and available for $9.99, every single day at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s? If your answer was a TJ’s Seasonal Bouquet you’d be correct! Take one home, trim its stems, arrange it in your favorite vase (see our TJ’s Bouquet Boost video for tips), and admire your blooms for days to come. Let their blossoming beauty remind you of a job well done… and a spring break well earned.

The snow is melting, the bees are abuzz—spring is near, and we like to think that warmer climes offer a chance to spring clean your wine selection. The season itself sings for something fresh & crisp, with a burst of acidity, like New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc—a “hills are alive”-worthy wine, if we do sing so ourselves (and, we do).

Situated in the northeast corner of New Zealand's South Island, the region of Marlborough has become synonymous with New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc, so revered for their output of fabulously bright & agreeably acidic wines of this variety. The moderate temps and ample sunshine allow for longer ripening of the grapes, concentrating their flavors to create highly sought-after wines with a characteristic zing.

And since your neighborhood Trader Joe’s is known for excellent values on highly sought-after wines from near and far (or very far, in this case), we’ve put together our top three Marlborough Sauvignon Blancs to help you ring in spring. We’ve even recommended a cheese board to go along with them, because, wine not?

No sense in beating around the bush—Picton Bay is the archetype of Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc, coming to our shelves from a family-owned and operated winery who’ve been in the wine business for over 25 years. The wine itself is made with 100% Sauvignon Blanc grapes, and pours with a pale gold hue. A single, vivid sip reveals fresh fruit aromas of lime, grapefruit and passion fruit, further buoyed by notes of crushed herbs and fresh cut grass, with a lingering finish.

Striking a balance between juiciness and minerality, a glass of Picton Bay shines alongside delicate grilled shellfish or pan-fried Trader Joe’s Branzino Fillets ($9.99 for 16 ounces) without overpowering it—we recommend a squeeze of lemon to further amp up the acidity factor. With similar wines selling elsewhere for $15 a bottle (or more), at Trader Joe’s we’ve chosen to strike a balance between high quality and tremendous value, by offering 750mL bottles of Picton Bay for the spring-in-your-step price of $7.99* each, everyday.

A returning favorite on our wine shelves for seven years (and counting!), The Pass is an exclusive-to-Trader-Joe’s wine that showcases everything the Marlborough growing region has to offer. Its straw yellow color and classically crisp, dry mouthfeel give way to highly aromatic grassy notes and lively tropical flavors, closely followed by hints of tongue-tingling, sweet-tart grapefruit—it’s akin to spring in a bottle.

The bracing acidity and fruit-forward nature of Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc, and the Pass in particular, provides excellent balance for spicy flavors and rich noodle dishes—which is why we love it paired with Trader Joe’s Peanut Udon Noodle Salad ($4.49 for 11.8 ounces) or Pad Thai ($2.99 for 10.5 ounces). And if that didn’t get your taste buds talking, our price makes it practically impossible to pass up: you’ll find 750mL bottles of The Pass at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s for $8.99* each, until we run out.

Our buyers traverse the globe in search of sip-worthy wine values to WOW our customers, and Sauvignon Republic is no exception to the rule. Pour a glass of this light yellow, 100% estate-grown Sauvignon Blanc and you’ll taste an eminently drinkable wine that’s aromatic and bright, offering intense tropical notes of kiwi and tangy grapefruit, with lush layers of white peach, underscored by a clean, refreshing finish. It’s no wonder we’ve brought new vintages to our shelves for 11 years and counting—it really is that good.

Sauvignon Republic’s mouthwatering minerality and fresh herb notes make it an elegant selection for springtime celebrations—it’s especially suited to green salads and crunchy crudites. If it’s a cheese board you’re after (and who isn’t?), the acidity of our creamy Goat Cheese with Fine Herbs ($2.99 for 5 ounces) creates an irresistibly invigorating pairing with the acidity of this wine. And at $7.99* per 750mL bottle, Sauvignon Republic is an especially irresistible value—one you’ll only find at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s.

blocks.description: Trader Joe’s Chevre Fine Herbs Goat Cheese has a uniquely herbaceous, tangy taste that separates it from just a traditional log of goat cheese. This lovely Chevre is fresh, soft, and unaged, and rolled in blend of parsley, basil, dill, tarragon, and chives, making it the perfect foil for snappy green veggies on a spring cheese board. Grab a glass of Sauvignon Blanc and toast to the start of the season!
blocks.title: Spring-y Goat Cheese Board

Picture this: the days are getting shorter, temperatures are falling, and you have a craving for a baked good to match the autumnal ambience. What’s a fall fanatic to do? Never fear! The dessert of your dreams is within reach—all it takes is a visit to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s and a box of Pumpkin Bread & Muffin Mix!

Arguably the originator of Trader Joe’s Pumpkin SeasonTJ, this peerless, pumpkin-packed Mix has been warming ovens and warding off snack attacks since 2008. Replete with dried pumpkin flakes and fantastic fall flourishes of cinnamon and nutmeg, you add the eggs, oil, and water, and the Mix does the heavy lifting, yielding a batch of moist Pumpkin Bread or fluffy Pumpkin Muffins with very little effort required on your part.

But aside from the obvious uses heralded in its name, this sweet, super versatile Mix's alter ego can be revealed with just a bit of recipe tinkering, resulting in delightfully chewy, splendidly aromatic Pumpkin Bars!

So how exactly does one turn bread into brownies? Allow us to elaborate: By reducing the water, replacing oil with butter, and adding a bit more sugar to the Mix, the batter bakes down into a dense, fudge-like bar, rather than a fluffy loaf. The result is a craveably chewy, pleasantly spiced bar that can be enjoyed as-is or garnished with a sweet, sour cream topping for a tangy, cooling counterpoint to the warm, seasonal spice profile. And if you’re feeling extra adventurous (you did just turn bread into brownies, after all), why not add chopped nuts, cranberries, or chocolate chips (or all three!) to the batter before baking?

blocks.description:
One of our favorite things about Trader Joe’s Pumpkin Bread and Muffin Mix is the way the subtle flavor of the pumpkin is perfectly complemented by the zesty additions of spices like cinnamon and nutmeg. Second to that fantastic flavor is its ease of use: Follow the package instructions and you’ll get a loaf of moist and fluffy, lightly spiced pumpkin bread, or a dozen standard-sized muffins, every time.

But if you’re seeking something even more dessert-y, say, for an after-dinner treat or booster club bake sale, you can follow the recipe below for a pumpkin bar of sorts that’s decidedly more “brownie” in texture than “bread.” The sweet, sour cream topping is by no means required, but will make these bars all the more delicious.
blocks.title: Pumpkin Bars

blocks.html: Whether you whip up a batch of bread, muffins, or bars, one box of this customer-favorite Mix has the power to squash pumpkin cravings for a whole crowd, for about the same price as one slice of a similar loaf at a coffee shop—a heroic value, if we’ve ever seen one. You’ll find Trader Joe’s Pumpkin Bread and Muffin Mix on the shelves with our other baking mixes, but only while the pumpkin posse is assembled in our stores.

Puff Pastry, also known as pâte feuilletée (meaning “leaf-like pastry”), bakes up to create an impossibly delicate and crisp exterior, with an interior that’s still airy and soft. Making such a pastry dough, however, is a painstakingly laborious and time-consuming process. Luckily, we’ve done the heavy lifting on this one, offering Trader Joe’s All Butter Puff Pastry Sheets in our frozen section for all the puff pastry projects of your holiday dreams!

Need some help getting your first ‘puff pastry projects’ started? You’re in luck! We’ve created two recipes using our Puff Pastry Sheets—one savory and one sweet—both of which will fit very nicely into a variety of celebratory eating opportunities that should arise this holiday season. Check out each recipe, then head to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s and grab whatever you need to make your Puff Pastry dreams a reality.

blocks.description:
For a festive dessert or decadent breakfast that looks like a winter wonderland, we’ve taken Trader Joe’s Puff Pastry Sheets and made them in to unique (and easy to make!) puff pastry “snowflakes,” then filled them with Trader Joe’s Cocoa Almond Spread. They’re finished with a dusting of powdered sugar for full snow effect.

Pro-tip: While you’re working with one sheet, keep the other in the refrigerator until ready to use. Chilled puff pastry is easier to work with than room temperature puff pastry.
blocks.title: Cocoa-Stuffed Snowflakes

blocks.description:
Looking for a showstopping appetizer for your next dinner or cocktail party? We’ve added pesto and ricotta cheese between two Trader Joe’s All Butter Puff Pastry Sheets for an impressive tear and share treat that’s as delicious to eat as it is delightful to look at.

Pro-tip: Chilled puff pastry is easier to work with than room temperature puff pastry. While you’re working with one sheet, keep the other in the refrigerator until ready to use.
blocks.title: Ricotta & Pesto Tear & Share

As the weather turns colder, our thoughts invariably turn to cozy cooking (we are a neighborhood grocery store, after all). And what better way to spend a chilly fall evening than to make—and eat!—a satisfying, saffron-infused rice cake made with Trader Joe’s pantry staples? 

While different cultures have their own iterations of the dish, our take on the classic Iranian tahchin [taah-cheen] takes its cues from the Persian version, and is sure to warm your kitchen and please your palate. Customarily, par-boiled rice—mixed with yogurt, egg, and saffron—is layered in a buttered pan with a savory sauté of meat or veggies, then covered and cooked on the stovetop or baked in the oven. 

This marriage of flavors is truly one to celebrate, but what really makes it special is the coveted golden crust (called “tahdig” [taah-deeg]) that develops on the outside as the tahchin cooks.

A welcoming, flavorful addition to a grateful gathering of family or friends (on the last Thursday in November, perhaps?), tahchin also makes a marvelous weeknight main when paired with a simple green salad.

Timid when it comes to tahchin construction? We’ve made a step-by-step video to guide you through it and ensure delicious results. Visit your neighborhood Trader Joe’s to grab the ingredients, then watch & follow the recipe—and tah-dig in!

blocks.description:
For a showstopping main or side dish, consider the Persian rice dish, Tahchin. Combine Trader Joe’s Basmati Rice with TJ’s Spanish Saffron, along with a few other everyday staples, like yogurt and eggs, and the result is an aromatic, golden-hued rice fit for any celebration-worthy occasion. 

Along with the saffron rice, the filling is bejewled with savory caramelized onion, nutty pistachios, tart TJ’s No Sugar Added Cranberries, and herby dill to really pack a punch of flavors. To successfully achieve the iconic golden, crispy exterior crust of the dish (called tahdig), opt for a generously buttered baking dish and the oven instead of the traditional stovetop method. Since that makes over half of the total recipe time hands-off (yes!), you need not wait for a special occasion to get in the kitchen and make this impressive dish. 

Don’t forget to save a bit of the caramelized onion filling to crown the top of your tahchin!
blocks.title: Baked & Bejeweled Tahchin

blocks.html: Basmati Rice has been grown for centuries in Northern India, near the foothills of the Himalayas. There, the soil conditions produce rice that is known for it’s nutty flavor, firm consistency, and distinctively floral aroma. It’s natural then that Trader Joe’s Basmati Rice (which we import from India), would deliver these same attractive qualities. And not only will it yield a tasty tahdig for your tahchin, but it’s also a fragrant foundation for coconut curry, shrimp jambalaya, rice pudding, pilaf, and more!

Saffron is the world’s most expensive spice, a direct result of the way it must be manually harvested, and the fact that only a few red ‘stigmas,’ can be culled from each Crocus sativus flower. Trader Joe’s Spanish Saffron is of the highest quality, while also appearing on our spice shelves with one of the lowest prices you’ll find anywhere. It also makes an appearance in your tahchin to impart an amber hue and warm, floral aroma.

Whether you’re new to the tofu club or a longtime supporter, you’ll find a dynamic roster in the refrigerators at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s. Our Organic High Protein Super Firm Tofu is an exemplary player, and a key component of our newest recipe for Katsu-style Soyaki Tofu.

Filling and flavorful, with a magnetic, “one-more-bite” appeal courtesy of its panko-powered crunch, this recipe takes tofu from building block to marvelous main. Watch the video, then head to Trader Joe’s to pick up the ingredients— you’d be hard-pressed to find better values elsewhere!

What makes Trader Joe’s Organic High Protein Super Firm Tofu so super? It’s made with organic sprouted soybeans, and more water is pressed out during production than standard tofu. This yields a dense (dare we say meat-like) texture that holds up beautifully when sautéed, grilled, or fried. Boasting an impressive 14 grams of protein per serving and a very mild flavor, this hearty Tofu is a must-have when making vegan katsu, and a proverbial blank slate for dips, sauces, and dressings of all kinds.

blocks.description:
Filling and flavorful, with a magnetic, “one-more-bite” appeal courtesy of its panko-powered crunch, this vegan, katsu-inspired recipe takes Trader Joe’s Organic High Protein Super Firm Tofu to flavorsome new heights. Traditionally, katsu is served with a sticky-sweet tonkatsu sauce (Japanese-style barbecue sauce); this recipe leans on Trader Joe’s Soyaki as both a marinade and a dipping sauce for ease of prep.

If you aren’t in the mood for rice and shredded cabbage, this crunchy, umami-infused tofu can be paired with the sides of your choosing (Riced Cauliflower and Baby Bok Choy, perhaps?). What’s more, the hands-free hour recommended to marinate the tofu allows you to relax with your latest read, squeeze in a workout, or simply decompress from the day before it’s time to fire up the air fryer or oven.
blocks.title: Katsu-style Soyaki Tofu

blocks.html: Speaking of sauces… Time and again, Trader Joe’s Soyaki has proven its mettle as a multipurpose meal enhancer. Boasting savory garlic and zesty ginger notes atop the faint sweetness of its soy sauce foundation, the addition of sesame seeds to the mix truly sets it apart from a typical teriyaki sauce. In this recipe, it pulls double-duty as a marinade and dipping sauce, and lends lip-smacking personality to the mild tofu.
