Nautically speaking, ‘sheets’ are ropes that steady the sail. When the sheets are not secured, sails flail unsteadily in the wind. In days of yore, this was a vivid metaphor for the drunken sailor who was often dubbed, “three sheets to the wind.” But in culinary terms, ‘sheets’ are large, rectangular pans that anchor your meal planning. With sheet-pan recipes as a regular part of your schedule, meal prep becomes—to borrow another nautical term—‘steady as she goes.’

Using some of our favorite Trader Joe’s products, we’ve lined up three recipes, each one entirely cooked on a single sheet pan. Prep the ingredients, position them on the pan, and push them into the oven for a trio of filling meals that are more than just a metaphor. We call them: “Three Sheets for the Win!” Watch the videos below, note the necessary ingredients, then sail on down to your neighborhood Trader Joe’s where you’ll find everything you need and more to keep your crew happy, and your household afloat!

The sheet pan is the unsung superstar in your kitchen—and this recipe is a one pan wonder! It offers a double dose of bright citrus—thanks to Trader Joe’s Cuban Style Citrusy Garlic Seasoning Blend and roasted Lemon wedges—and is full of different textured veggies that a sheet pan can easily accommodate.

Pair with BBQ Cut Fresh Atlantic Salmon, not only because it makes a filling, flavorful meal, but because the entire sheet pan is ready at the same time—a welcomed option for weeknight meals when time is tight, and your culinary enthusiasm is low. And don’t forget a hefty drizzle of Chimichurri Sauce to make this sheet pan really sing!

When you see the Trader Joe’s name on a package, you can be assured that what's inside contains colors derived only from naturally available products. We take this commitment seriously, and it only seems fitting to extend said commitment to creative culinary pursuits as well—like dyeing Easter Eggs!

Whether you’re the mastermind behind this year’s Easter egg hunt or you’re simply looking to spruce up your space with eggs-quisite, DIY décor, follow this video or the instructions below to see just how easy it is to dye eggs naturally with a few Trader Joe’s products—no artificial food coloring required!

blocks.title: How To Dye Eggs Naturally With Trader Joe's Products

blocks.html:
How to dye eggs naturally with Trader Joe’s products:

  1. Combine 4 cups (1 quart) of water and 2 tablespoons TJ's White Modena Vinegar in a medium pot.
  2. Bring water to a boil and add dye ingredients as follows for your preferred egg color (If you want them all, you’ll need to make multiple batches):
    • For yellow: 3 tablespoons TJ’s Organic Ground Turmeric
    • For blue: 1 package TJ’s Frozen Blueberries
    • For green: 2 cups TJ’s Organic Pomegranate Juice
    • For pink: 2 cups chopped TJ’s Fresh Organic Beets
  3. Lower heat and simmer dye for 30 minutes, let cool.
  4. If using beets or blueberries, strain and reserve dye (eat the beets, if you like).
  5. Add hard-boiled eggs to large glass jars or containers (don't use plastic—it will stain!). Fill jars with cooled dye to cover eggs.
  6. Let eggs sit anywhere from 30 minutes to a few hours to take on the desired color—the longer they sit, the deeper the color.
  7. Remove eggs and pat dry with paper towels.
  8. Happy hunting!

blocks.html: A hodgepodge mixture. An awkward, hasty movement on rough ground. An order bunch of out words of. When it comes to defining “scramble,” it’s not always pleasant. When we’re talking about food, though, it’s a delight! And while eggs are normally the go-to ingredient for scrambling purposes, variety is truly the spice of life. So, why not take a cue from this recipe video for tofu breakfast tacos (starring none other than Trader Joe’s Organic Tofu) and shake up your morning routine?

How do these breakfast tacos get their heft? Made with organic soybeans, a three-ounce serving of Trader Joe’s Organic Tofu contains six grams of protein—that’s the same amount you’d find in a large egg, but with fewer calories and fat than said egg. Yes! 

And crumbling a block of this Organic Tofu produces a texture that resembles scrambled eggs. Double yes!

A liberal application of savory seasonings (including garlic powder, onion powder, and TJ’s Nutritional Yeast) ensures maximum flavor in the finished scramble, and a pinch of turmeric provides its characteristically sunny hue. The mixture is sautéed until golden brown, at which point you’ve got the hearty base of a breakfast taco (or breakfast burrito, or breakfast bowl) on your hands. And don’t forget the pico de gallo, fresh cilantro, and sliced avocado—garnishes are key to creating the full breakfast taco experience!

blocks.description: It's breakfast time—and instead of breaking eggs, we're crumbing a block of tofu! It turns out crumbled Trader Joe's Organic Tofu possesses the same soft, curd-like texture of fluffy scrambled eggs. And when it's seasoned with garlic powder, onion powder, and TJ’s Nutritional Yeast (plus a pinch of turmeric for its characteristically sunny hue), then sautéed until piping hot, this Tofu scramble can be served like any traditional scramble: on its own, over toast, or in these breakfast tacos. Good morning, indeed!

Whether your Thanksgiving traditions include a fancy, formal feast or an informal gathering of friends, roasting a turkey for the Big Meal can be intimidating... but it doesn’t have to be!  

Gather your people, follow our step-by-step TJ’s Turkey Roasting Guide, and not only will you have a boast-worthy bird, but you’ll also be considered (by us) a certified Trader Joe’s Roastmaster. Which, of course, is what you’ve always wanted. You’ve got this. Let’s begin!

There are several items you’re going to need to successfully roast your turkey, first and foremost being, well, the turkey! Luckily, whole, fresh Turkeys will be touching down at your neighborhood Trader Joe’s on Thursday, November 13th. Trader Joe’s Turkeys are... 

  • Selected from young hens (no toms), ensuring tender, juicy meat
  • Raised in the U.S. in large, open-air grow houses
  • Vegetarian-fed, minimally processed, and never given antibiotics
  • 100% fresh (never frozen!)

This year, we have three different birds to choose from:

• 1 stick TJ’s Unsalted Butter, softened
  • 1 package each of TJ’s Fresh Sage, Rosemary, & Thyme
  • TJ’s Sea Salt & TJ’s Black Pepper, to taste
  • 1-2 TJ’s Yellow Onions, peeled & quartered
  • 1-2 TJ’s Lemons, quartered
  • Kitchen twine

Using a food processor, or by hand, chop a third of each package of fresh TJ’s Sage, Rosemary & Thyme. Mix herbs, salt, pepper and butter until well combined. Place mixture on parchment paper and roll into a log. Refrigerate until firm.

Our turkeys are never frozen, but we do keep them super cold. Plan to buy your bird in advance, and keep it in the refrigerator. 

On T-Day, take the turkey out of the fridge and unwrap and remove the temporary wire truss. Locate and remove the neck & giblets, then set them aside for potential future use (stuffing, gravy, soup, gumbo, etc.) Don’t see them? If you’ve selected one of our birds that “may contain giblets” (as marked on the label), it’s possible that your bird doesn’t have them—but check the bird’s back end just in case. 

Loosen skin by gently sliding your fingers between the skin and breast and working them down to the thigh (note: gentleness is key to avoid puncturing the skin).  

Cut 3/4 of your Herby Compound Butter into disks. Rub 1 disk on outer skin (to encourage crispness) and carefully push and mush the remainder under the skin. Stuff the cavity with onions, lemons and the bundle of herbs. Melt remaining herb butter for basting and set aside.

Finally, truss the bird. Why truss? Trussing the bird ensures even cooking and ease of carving. Preheat your oven to 400°F. Then, truss the bird according to your tradition. 

You can keep it loose by tucking the wings snugly under the bird and tying the legs together, making sure the skin flap gets tucked up between them. (You can watch this method in our Turkey Roasting video.) Or you can construct an elaborate harness for the bird. It’s up to you... just bring the twine and the attitude! We trussed you.

Place your turkey in a 400°F oven and roast 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, turn the heat down to 325ºF. After 1 hour, baste every 30 minutes with reserved melted herb butter. 

At 2 hours, or when bird reaches desired color, tent with foil to slow browning. Continue checking the temperature in the thickest part of bird (the thigh), taking care not to let your meat thermometer touch bone. Cooking time depends on the bird’s size (see chart below), your oven’s temperament, and other unforeseen variables. 

Your turkey is done when the thermometer registers 165ºF and the juices run clear from the bird. Finally, let the bird rest for 20-30 minutes prior to carving. Happy Thanksgiving!

It’s true: we’re awfully fond of fondue. Especially so during the holidays—just the idea of a pot of marvelously melty cheese is enough to make us feel as cozy as can be. In that spirit, we offer some seriously convenient heat-and-serve fondue options this time of year, and a whole host of cheeses with which to make some yourself.

Here, we’ve assembled some tips to maximize your melting enjoyment, including a few fon-do’s and fon-don’ts, as well as a recipe for an easy fondue for two. Get your long forks ready, slice up an apple or two, and join us for a festive fête of molten fromage, as we show how We Fondue—and You Can, Too!

Captured here demonstrating a gloriously gooey cheese pull, Trader Jacques’ La Fondue comes to us from the French Alps, where Gruyere, Emmental and Comté cheeses are crafted from the milk of cows grazed on lush alpine grasses. When heated through, this Fondue becomes beautifully bubbly, alluringly aromatic with notes of crisp white wine, and ideal for all sorts of dipping. Best of all, you can prep it in the microwave in five minutes, and if convenience is paramount, you can even serve it in its own package!

We recommend enjoying it with anything from bread cubes and cornichons, ham and salami, veggies and fruit… Oh, the possibilities! We’re selling each 17.9-ounce microwavable cup of Trader Jacques’ La Fondue for the super price of $7.99. Now through the holidays, you’ll find it in our cheese case.
Now, if you elect to forge your own fondue, fear not! It’s a surprisingly simple process, particularly when you follow these tried-and-true tips:

It's a Breeze With Shredded Cheese

Take some of the work off your hands by incorporating our pre-shredded cheeses into the equation—our Shredded Swiss Cheese & Gruyère Cheese, in particular, is a reason to be grateful not to grate. 

Have Fun With Flavor

For a tasty twist, we recommend using some of our fantastically full-flavored cheeses in concert with fondue classics like Emmentaler and Comté—a bit of our Shredded Pizza Seasoned Toscano, Cheddar with Caramelized Onions, or Italian Truffle Cheese will bring your fondue to bold new frontiers.

Fiery Fondue for Two

Combining the cool creaminess of Fontina with the peppery heat of our Cheddar Cheese with Scotch Bonnet Chili and Red Peppers, this easy recipe is just the thing to keep you and a loved one warm for a winter’s evening at home.

Not sure what to dip? How about a lightly toasted cubes of TJ's Organic Baguette, crisp apple slices, bite-sized roasted potatoes, tangy TJ's Cornichons...

You may be thinking: What kind of whirled cups can I make using Trader Joe’s products? A better question might be: What kind of whirled cups CAN’T you make? Your neighborhood TJ’s is stocked with ALL the ingredients guaranteed to give your amateur blended game a promotion—all the way up to the top bracket!

With that goal in mind, we’re pitching a hat-trick of banger recipes below. Although, you’re not just relegated to these. (In fact, there’s absolutely no penalty if you start with a clean sheet and take a shot at creating a brand new recipe.) If you need a kick-start, see our Alternates & Super Subs ingredients (scroll down), then head to Trader Joe’s so you can make your next whirled cup a win to remember!

Every wholesome smoothie kicks-off with a liquid foundation: juice, milk, water... Our Blueberry Oat Smoothie recipe begins with Trader Joe’s Oat Beverage. This Non-Dairy player exhibits a delightfully smooth, “creamy” texture, and mildly sweet flavor that comes, not from added cane sugar (as with other brands), but with sugar derived from hydrolyzing the Oats (breaking down the starches with water). In the recipe, this dairy free, lactose free, gluten free, vegan base is matched with our Frozen Blueberries and other simple ingredients to create an energizing smoothie that helps you stand up to the competition, no matter what the rest of your day holds in store. Take it for a whirl!

These Cuties don’t just dazzle with their looks; when in play, they display some serious moves—sweet, natural flavors with notes of citrus and lemongrass, plus a truly resonant crunch.
